chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Jarrah al-Mad'ini, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Eat on the day of al-Fitr before you pray, and do not eat on the day of al-Adha until the Imam departs."

key_terms.يَنْصَرِفَ الْإِمَامُ: The Imam departs/finishes (referring to the conclusion of the Eid prayer)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْأَضْحَى: The day of Eid al-Adha (the Festival of Sacrifice)
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْفِطْرِ: The day of Eid al-Fitr (celebrating the end of Ramadan)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating before the Eid prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* codifies the Sunnah of contrasting the two Eids: eating before Fitr prayer emphasizes the end of Ramadan's fast, while delaying food until after Adha prayer aligns with the Prophet’s practice of sacrificing his first animal. This distinction highlights the jurisprudential nuance between the celebratory nature of Fitr and the ritualistic solemnity of Adha within Shia fiqh.
